bull_bear.body: Net cash Rs 3,990 cr; disciplined capital allocation emphasised. Capex Rs 320 cr funded internally. Continued investment in distribution, brand/A&P (rising in FMEG), product innovation and talent. No buyback/dividend specifics on this call.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Volume deceleration optics:** 3 straight quarters of modest volume (low-to-mid-single-digit) — management insists it's base effects + RM-price-driven de-stocking, not demand loss; verify over 10-12 months.
- **T&D/data-center timing risk:** an analyst pushed that CEA T&D targets have historically undershot (14k vs 23k), and 1 GW/yr data-center adds are too small to move a ~Rs 1 lakh cr TAM — execution/timing is the swing factor.
- **Export/geopolitics:** Middle East (Strait of Hormuz, Iran-US) hit exports; resurfaced last week — recovery not linear.
- **Commodity volatility:** copper/aluminium swings drive channel stocking and near-term realizations; a 3-4% price cut already taken in July.
- **Margin sustainability:** FMEG 8% EBIT is at the FY30 floor already — seasonality could pull it back; W&C export drag persists.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident, data-rich, willing to "agree and disagree" with skeptical analysts (T&D debate). Transparent about volume being modest and the reasons (base + de-stocking). Consistent reaffirmation of Project Spring guardrails rather than chasing the strong print. By-design refusal to split FMEG category revenues or give copper/Q2 price guidance. Macro preamble is thorough (Fed/BoE/RBI, oil, IMF).
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The headline +39%/+43% W&C growth is realization-led, not volume-led (volume only low-to-mid-single-digit) — commodity tailwind flatters the top line; watch volume as the true share signal.
- The 15-day working-capital cycle is a temporary LC/payables artefact, not a structural improvement — it reverts to 45-50 days.
- FMEG's re-rating is real: solar inverter went from 3rd-largest to largest FMEG category in a year and EBIT hit the FY30 floor 4 years early — but still <50% of FMEG and seasonality-exposed.
- Bharat Net fibre is fully pre-secured for 3 years — Polycab is NOT exposed to the current fibre-price spike, unlike fibre-buying EPC peers.
- Channel de-stocking on falling RM prices means reported sell-in likely understates true sell-out this quarter — a possible coiled spring if prices stabilise.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- The balance sheet is effectively debt-free at the funded level — non-current borrowings of ₹358 Mn and short-term borrowings of ₹694 Mn against total shareholder funds of ₹1,21,010 Mn.
- The company holds a net cash position of ₹39,900 Mn (cash, investments and non-current deposits less debt), giving it self-funding capacity for the capex programme.
- A large and growing acceptances balance (₹51,408 Mn at Jun-26 vs ₹25,668 Mn a year earlier) is the primary working-capital funding lever, with the associated cost showing up in finance charges on LC/VBD rather than bank interest.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Market leadership in W&C: India's No.1 cables and wires company with 30-31% share of the organised market, scale nearly twice its peers, ~10,000 SKUs, and industry-leading EBIT margins
- Well-footed FMEG player: scaled to Rs 20,693 million in FY26 at a 25% CAGR since FY2013-14, six-category portfolio with 5,200+ SKUs
- Pan-India distribution network: 3,900+ dealers and distributors, 190,000+ retail outlets, 24-hour delivery system, omnichannel presence (e-commerce, modern trade, mobile app)
- High degree of backward integration: 100% of C&W sales manufactured in-house, improving quality control, margins and supply continuity
- Strong R&D capabilities: NABL ISO 17025-certified R&D centre developing eco-friendly and E-beam-irradiated cables via global polymer research collaborations
- Quality/promoter-led management team providing long-term vision and stewardship, backed by an experienced, independent Board
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw-material commodity price volatility — Copper, aluminium, PVC and steel prices were volatile through FY26 on supply-side disruptions (an Indonesian mining landslide, Middle East smelting/petrochemical disruptions) and demand shifts; as key cable/wire inputs, sustained volatility pressures input costs and margins despite hedging and pricing actions.
- Currency depreciation — The Indian rupee depreciated significantly against the US dollar during FY26 (from ~85.5/USD in April 2025 to above 93-95/USD by fiscal year-end), driven by crude prices, capital flows and trade-policy shifts, raising import costs for USD-denominated commodity inputs.
- Global trade protectionism and tariffs — Expanding US tariffs and non-tariff measures (anti-dumping duties, safeguard actions), alongside similar measures by other economies, are accelerating trade fragmentation and regionalisation of supply chains, which can affect export competitiveness and merchandise-export demand relevant to Polycab's international business.
- Geopolitical disruption in the Middle East — Escalating Middle East tensions disrupted aluminium smelting and petrochemical (PVC feedstock) supply chains during the year and directly impacted Polycab's export sales in Q4 FY26, evidencing the Company's exposure to geopolitical shocks in a key international market.
- China and global macro slowdown — China's economy expanded only moderately (~4.5%-5.0%) amid real-estate-sector stress and local government debt concerns, while the Eurozone saw subdued growth (~0.8%-1.2%) with manufacturing weakness in economies such as Germany; a weaker global environment can weigh on demand in Polycab's international/export markets.
- Dependence on India's infrastructure and government capex cycle — Domestic W&C and FMEG demand growth is closely tied to sustained government infrastructure/capital expenditure, private-sector capex revival and real-estate activity; a slowdown in any of these domestic growth drivers would directly affect Polycab's core revenue base.

business.body:

business.body:
- The business is presented as three reported segments — Wires & Cables (the dominant revenue engine), FMEG, and EPC — with W&C growth attributed to resilient domestic demand rather than a single end-market.
- Alongside the domestic franchise, the company maintains an international/export business that the deck frames as a diversified global footprint with a healthy order book, though export contribution to revenue remains low single digit.
- Strategy is explicitly organised around 'Project Spring', a named multi-year programme with published segment-level targets extending to FY30.
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Ownership] Promoter holding stands at 61% as on 30 June 2026, with FII at 19%, DII at 5% and QIB/AIF at 3% — a promoter-controlled, institutionally supported register.
- [Input-cost risk] The safe harbour explicitly names international copper, aluminium and oil prices as key swing factors, confirming commodity pass-through as a structural feature of the business model.
- [Advertising] Brand spend is being scaled alongside the FMEG push, with advertisement and sales promotion expense of ₹328 Mn in the quarter versus ₹150 Mn in the year-ago period.

business.body: Polycab manufactures wires and cables (W&C, ~87% of revenue) for infrastructure, power, industrial, real-estate and mobility customers, and Fast-Moving Electrical Goods (FMEG, ~7% of revenue) including fans, lighting and luminaires, solar products, switchgear, switches, conduit pipes/fittings and small domestic appliances for retail and commercial customers. It also runs an Engineering, Procurement & Construction (EPC) division executing electrical infrastructure projects for government and institutional power customers. Products are sold domestically through an omnichannel dealer/distributor/retail network and exported to 94 countries.

latest_quarter.body: W&C margin is a function of four levers: (1) export contribution (a drag this quarter on Middle East), (2) wires-vs-cables mix (wires higher-margin, helped), (3) channel-vs-institutional (channel higher, helped), (4) operating leverage (muted this quarter). Net, margins were "supported" at 13.3% despite the export drag. FMEG margin (8%) driven by operating leverage on a low base + premium-mix step-up (25% overall). Cost-plus model on copper/aluminium — RM moves pass through with a lag; falling June prices dampened channel stocking.
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Revenue +39% YoY (~Rs 8,210 cr implied); EBITDA margin 13.8% (+70 bps QoQ); PAT Rs 796.7 cr (+33% YoY, highest-ever), 9.7% margin; net cash Rs 3,990 cr; capex Rs 320 cr; WC cycle 15 days (temporary). W&C +39% (domestic +43%, volume low-to-mid-single-digit on ~26% base; EBIT 13.3%). FMEG +71% (EBIT 8%, solar >2x, premium mix 25%). EPC -11% YoY (timing; EBIT 11%). Exports down on Middle East; 3-4% price cut taken early July. Guidance reaffirmed: 1.5x-market volume, W&C 11-13%, FMEG 8-10% by FY30, exports >10% of topline by 2030.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: volume growth re-acceleration as base eases + post-price-cut restocking; export recovery (US/Middle East order book conversion); EPC revenue catch-up (Bharat Net Rs 800-1,000 cr / RDSS Rs 800 cr FY27 pace); FMEG margin holding ~8% through seasonality; WC cycle normalizing toward 45-50 days; data-center order translation._

outlook.body:
- **Volume growth:** 1.5x market/industry growth (blend of volume & value), reaffirmed through FY30; FY26 delivered 18% volume growth as the reference.
- **W&C margin:** 11-13% EBIT medium-to-long term (Project Spring); Q1 at 13.3% (top of band).
- **FMEG:** grow 1.5x-2x industry; EBITDA margin 8-10% by FY30 (EBIT already 8% this quarter — running ahead, but seasonality caveated).
- **EPC:** sustainable operating margin high-single-digit (Q1 at 11%, above trend); FY27 revenue ~Rs 800-1,000 cr from Bharat Net + ~Rs 800 cr from RDSS.
- **Exports:** >10% of consolidated topline by 2030 (export growth to outpace domestic); "uncapped" opportunity, no hard target.
- **Working capital:** settle back to 45-50 days.

Exports: "very healthy" order book across US, Europe, LatAm; US ~45-50% of export turnover, Europe ~18-20%, Middle East ~20-24% (Oman/Saudi/UAE recovering). outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **T&D/grid capex:** CEA guides ~20,000-21,000 circuit-km/yr for FY26-30 (vs ~14-15k last 5 yrs); FY27 ~17,000 ckm, with 2,000 ckm already added in Apr-May. Rs 100 spent on T&D ≈ 15% cable content (high pull-through). Transformer peers' order books at ~2.5x revenue cited as a lead indicator.
- **Rooftop solar:** PM Surya Ghar Yojana + state/central incentives driving the solar-inverter engine; 2-3 year strong trajectory expected.
- **Data centres / defence / EV charging:** ~4-5% of demand today, flagged as a potential "another layer" of demand that could explode.
- **Manufacturing/private capex:** BSE-500 ex-BFSI committed ~Rs 11.6 lakh cr capex over next 12-18 months (metals, semiconductors, manufacturing, renewables).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Project Spring: five-year strategic roadmap to FY 2029-30 built around solidifying B2B leadership in W&C, scaling the FMEG/B2C consumer business, ramping up international business, capacity expansion and cost/backward-integration discipline
- B2B: scale into large multi-decade infrastructure opportunities (power transmission, renewable energy integration, semiconductors, data centres, urban infrastructure, defence and aerospace) leveraging manufacturing depth, product range and institutional relationships
- B2C/FMEG: translate cables-and-wires brand credibility into a full-spectrum consumer electrical brand (fans, switches, lighting) anchored on a 'Quality, Service and Delivery' (QSD) philosophy
- FMEG go-to-market: institutionalise a micro-market strategy segmenting the country into high-potential geographic clusters for localised marketing, product positioning and distribution, complemented by an influencer management program targeting electricians, contractors and retailers
- International expansion: deepen presence in overseas markets through calibrated market development, customer engagement, product approvals/certifications and deeper engagement with large EPC players, aiming to build a profitable and resilient international franchise
- Cables and wires innovation: pursue growth 'beyond the core' in electric vehicles/EV charging, defence and marine (naval/submarine cables), and data centres as incremental demand segments, backed by the Polymer R&D Centre
- Retail wires: network optimisation and expansion into 'grey and white spaces', aggressive premiumisation anchored on the Green Wire+ product line, supported by the 'No Compromise' brand safety campaign
- Solar business unit: build complete in-house manufacturing for the full range of string inverters and expand into Hybrid Inverters and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to strengthen presence in distributed energy and backup power
- Fans: transition portfolio toward premium and energy-efficient (BLDC) offerings and upgrade products to meet updated BEE Star energy-efficiency norms
- Succession and leadership: strengthen leadership depth via the appointment of Joint Managing Directors, a CEO for the B2B Channel business, and a Chief Digital & Information Officer to support technology/digitisation-led scaling
- Capital allocation: fund capacity expansion primarily through internal accruals while progressively increasing the dividend payout ratio
- Polycab funds its capacity expansion primarily through internal accruals given its net-cash balance sheet, positioning the Company to self-fund future investments while continuing to deliver returns to shareholders. For FY 2025-26 the Board recommended a dividend for the year, does not propose to transfer any amount to Reserves, and the Company has not accepted any public deposits. The Company also maintains enterprise-wide certification to ISO 9001 (QMS), ISO 14001 (EMS), ISO 45001 (OHMS), ISO 50001 (EnMS), ISO 17025, IATF 16949 and IRIS as part of its quality/operational-resilience commitment underpinning Project Spring.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Polycab operates 26 manufacturing plants across India (including named sites at Halol & Daman, Roorkee, Nashik, Chennai and Bangalore), supported by 35 warehouses/depots and a corporate, EPC and Telecom office network. Under the five-year 'Project Spring' plan (to FY 2029-30), the Company plans to invest Rs 60-80 billion in capital expenditure over the next five years, focused on capacity expansion, backward integration, digitization and ESG-led initiatives. During FY 2025-26 it incurred capital expenditure of approximately Rs 14.8 billion, its highest-ever annual capex, directed primarily at capacity-expansion initiatives and funded through internal accruals given its net-cash balance sheet. In the Solar business unit, manufacturing capacity was scaled up during the year (string inverter production raised to 1 million units annually; Solar Box production raised from 25,000 to 60,000 units/month), and for FY 2026-27 the Company is targeting complete in-house manufacturing of its full range of solar string inverters plus the launch of Hybrid Inverters and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS). Separately, Polycab has entered a major indigenisation programme for pressure-tight submarine cables for naval projects (destroyers, frigates, aircraft carriers), with long-term testing running until April 2027.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- India's economy expected to sustain growth momentum (GDP projected 6.5%-7.5% ahead) supported by infrastructure investment, policy continuity and favourable demographics, providing a resilient domestic demand backdrop
- Global cables and wires market is structurally attractive, underpinned by grid modernisation and clean-energy investment in the US, EU, China and the Middle East, renewable capacity additions, data-centre/digital-infrastructure growth, EV adoption and urbanisation
- Indian W&C industry demand growth is estimated at approximately 1.5x-2.0x real GDP, driven by power transition (T&D expansion, grid modernisation, underground cabling), renewable energy evacuation infrastructure, infrastructure development, real-estate/housing wires demand, a gradual revival in private capex, and structural formalisation favouring organised/branded players
- Broader FMEG/electricals industry (fans, lighting, pumps, switches & switchgears) expected to grow at ~6-7% CAGR over CY25-29, driven by urbanisation, rising electrification and disposable incomes, premiumisation and adoption of energy-efficient/smart/IoT products; discretionary retail demand was mixed (weather variability, cautious spending) while institutional/commercial/project-led demand was stable
- W&C segment growth in FY26 was driven by robust domestic demand, particularly government infrastructure investment in mobility and power, and steady real-estate activity; product mix shifted toward cables (over wires) on higher infrastructure/industrial demand
- Commodity input costs remained volatile: copper supported by an Indonesian mining-landslide supply shock and structurally strong electrification/renewable/EV demand; aluminium supported by Middle East smelting disruptions and limited capacity expansion; PVC saw an initial correction followed by a supply-driven recovery tied to Middle East feedstock disruption; steel moved cyclically on trade measures; the rupee depreciated meaningfully against the US dollar over the year, adding to input-cost and margin pressure
- International business growth was affected by Middle East tensions that impacted export sales in Q4, though management remains confident in the long-term export outlook given a healthy order book and supportive demand trends across renewables, power infrastructure, oil & gas and data centres
- FMEG growth was driven by business restructuring, distributor/channel expansion, new SKU launches and brand-building, with the segment turning sustainably profitable after breaking even in Q4FY25
- Polycab's international/export business carries a healthy order book with supportive demand trends, despite Middle East tensions impacting Q4 export sales
- In EPC, Polycab is executing two key government-aligned infrastructure projects — BharatNet and the Revamped Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS) — with execution under BharatNet commencing during FY26

Wires & Cables domestic grew +43% YoY (though volumes only low-to-mid-single-digit on a ~26% base, so growth is commodity/realization-heavy), and FMEG roared +71% YoY (10th straight quarter beating industry) led by solar inverters (>2x) with EBIT already at 8% — the FY30 Project-Spring floor. Exports dipped on the Middle East, but management guides recovery with a healthy US/Europe/LatAm order book. All medium-term guardrails (W&C 11-13% EBIT, FMEG 8-10% EBITDA by FY30, 1.5x-market volume growth) reaffirmed.

risks.note: Copper, aluminium, PVC and steel prices were volatile through FY26 on supply-side disruptions (an Indonesian mining landslide, Middle East smelting/petrochemical disruptions) and demand shifts; as key cable/wire inputs, sustained volatility pressures input costs and margins despite hedging and pricing actions.

The Indian rupee depreciated significantly against the US dollar during FY26 (from ~85.5/USD in April 2025 to above 93-95/USD by fiscal year-end), driven by crude prices, capital flows and trade-policy shifts, raising import costs for USD-denominated commodity inputs.

Expanding US tariffs and non-tariff measures (anti-dumping duties, safeguard actions), alongside similar measures by other economies, are accelerating trade fragmentation and regionalisation of supply chains, which can affect export competitiveness and merchandise-export demand relevant to Polycab's international business.

Escalating Middle East tensions disrupted aluminium smelting and petrochemical (PVC feedstock) supply chains during the year and directly impacted Polycab's export sales in Q4 FY26, evidencing the Company's exposure to geopolitical shocks in a key international market.
risks.risk: Geopolitical disruption in the Middle East

risks.note: China's economy expanded only moderately (~4.5%-5.0%) amid real-estate-sector stress and local government debt concerns, while the Eurozone saw subdued growth (~0.8%-1.2%) with manufacturing weakness in economies such as Germany; a weaker global environment can weigh on demand in Polycab's international/export markets.

Domestic W&C and FMEG demand growth is closely tied to sustained government infrastructure/capital expenditure, private-sector capex revival and real-estate activity; a slowdown in any of these domestic growth drivers would directly affect Polycab's core revenue base.
risks.risk: Dependence on India's infrastructure and government capex cycle
